children: Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials) spent much of the summer going nowhere. Goldman Sachs thinks that might be changing.

Micron and SanDisk both climbed more than 1% in Tuesday premarket trade as a rally in memory stocks moved from Asia to the U.S. moves were much bigger in this country. SK Hynix rose 8.2% and Samsung Electronics added 5.6%. Again it's the commerce that's led by AI.
Powerful models need a lot of memory and GPUs, which is driving the demand for high bandwidth memory, DRAM, and data center storage. Goldman has seen early signs of investor re-engagement.

Micron and SanDisk are beginning to break out of the downtrends that held them back over the summer, the firm said. Hedge fund positioning is still rather small and volatility in semiconductors has also dropped to about 36 from 65 in July. What matters is the mixture.
If demand for AI memory stays robust, investors that scaled back exposure during the summer might have a chance to recover positions.
The basic backdrop has already been improving as AI data centers gobble up more and more memory and storage. But memory is still a circular business.

Prices, supply increases and consumer spending can fluctuate quickly, so a technical breakout needs earnings backing. The company's next big test comes when it announces fiscal fourth-quarter results Sept. 30. That report should tell us if the latest memory boom has sufficient profit growth behind it to keep it continuing.

title: Goldman Says the Worst May Be Over for Micron and SanDisk
